name: Aurobindo Ghosh
role: Indian nationalist leader (1905-1910), later yogi and philosopher (1872-1950)
summary: Aurobindo was an early leader of the Indian nationalist movement who demanded complete autonomy, boycott and passive resistance (with armed revolt among the legitimate options), and after 1910 withdrew to Pondicherry to develop Integral Yoga. His political writings describe nationalism as a spiritual calling, warn against totalitarian collectivism and the sufficiency of reason, favour free self-determination of nations within an eventual world-union, and support the Allied cause in the Second World War.
